Nollywood actress and filmmaker, Funke Akindele, has backed the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu’s directive urging hospitals to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports. Akindele expressed her support in a post on her X account on Saturday, while sharing a video of the Nigeria Police Force’s message on the directive. Addressing doctors and other healthcare workers, she urged them to begin treatment immediately whenever a gunshot victim was brought to their facilities, rather than insist on police documentation. “To our doctors and health workers, the Inspector-General of Police has said it clearly. “When someone comes to you with a gunshot wound, please begin treatment immediately. You don’t need to ask for a police report before you attend to them. Treat first. Save lives first,” she wrote. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources She also encouraged members of the public to help injured persons get to hospitals, assuring them that the police had a responsibility to protect lives. “To everyone watching, if you see someone who’s been shot, please don’t be afraid to help them get to a hospital. “The duty of the police is to protect lives, and I commend the Nigeria Police Force for making that clear,” she added. Akindele called on Nigerians to support efforts to save lives, saying, “Let’s help save lives. That’s what matters most.” PUNCH Online had reported that IG Tunji Disu urged hospitals and medical personnel across the country to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports before providing medical attention. https://punchng.com/no-police-report-required-before-treating-gunshot-victims-ig/ “When a gunshot victim is brought to any hospital, the law does not require a police report before treatment,” he said. He also appealed to doctors and healthcare workers to prioritise saving lives, while encouraging members of the public to assist injured persons in emergencies. “To members of the public, if you see someone injured, do not hesitate to help. You will not be punished for helping,” Disu said. He concluded with a call to hospitals and emergency responders: “Treat first, save lives.” Tosin Oyediran Tosin Oyediran is a journalist with Punch Newspapers, bringing over eight years of newsroom experience to his coverage of politics, health, advocacy, sports, and entertainment.
